title: Tipu Sultan: Villain or Hero?
byline: an anthology, with a note by Sita Ram Goel · Voice of India · 1993
lede: In 1989–90 Doordarshan screened The Sword of Tipu Sultan, Sanjay Khan's serial based on Bhagwan Gidwani's novel, which presented Tipu as a secular, benevolent patriot. Writers from Kerala, Karnataka and Maharashtra objected. This anthology gathers their essays, mostly from Malayalam, Kannada and Marathi papers, and the record of their campaign and court case. Their counter-portrait of Tipu draws on his own letters and seal, his court historians, and the Malabar and Mysore gazetteers. In Malabar and Coorg, they argue, his rule meant forced conversion, destroyed temples and renamed towns.
facts: of Tipu's reign, 7 December 1782 to 4 May 1799

essays and records, plus appendices on the Mappilas, the Travancore lines and the court order
note: Tipu's record is genuinely contested. Many historians stress his wars against the British, his modernising administration and his grants to temples such as Sringeri. These contributors emphasise the violence in Malabar and Coorg recorded in the sources. This page sets out the anthology's case and sources, attributed to its authors.
